'''Shankar Ghosh''' (born 28 June 1975) is an Indian physicist, currently associated at the Department of Condensed Matter Physics and Material Science, [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]]. He is known for his research on experimental condensed matter physics. The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]] for his contributions to physical sciences in 2019.<ref name="ssb.webpage">{{Cite web|url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/Detail.aspx?AID=560|title=Awardee Details: Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize|website=ssbprize.gov.in|access-date=2020-03-22}}</ref>

== Awards ==
In 2019, Ghosh was awarded the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology for his innovative and unconventional experiments on soft matter.<ref name="ssb.webpage" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/two-from-iit-bombay-1-from-tifr-get-coveted-science-award/articleshow/71346466.cms|title=Two from IIT-Bombay, 1 from TIFR get coveted science award |date=September 28, 2019|website=The Times of India|language=en|access-date=2020-03-22}}</ref> The following year, Ghosh became a laureate of the [[Asian Scientist 100]] by the ''[[Asian Scientist]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.asianscientist.com/as100/ |title=The Asian Scientist 100 |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= |website= |publisher= [[Asian Scientist]] |access-date= 13 March 2025 |quote= |language= }}</ref>
